title: Jeonju vs Busan: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Jeonju for food culture and hanok atmosphere; Busan for beaches, seafood, and city variety. Do both on the Seoul–Jeonju–Busan circuit.

categories.name: Food Culture
categories.summary: Jeonju is Korea's food capital — bibimbap birthplace, kongnamul gukbap, and legendary makgeolli bars with free food.

categories.name: Beaches
categories.summary: Jeonju is landlocked. Busan has Haeundae and Gwangalli.

categories.name: Traditional Atmosphere
categories.summary: 735 hanok buildings, the largest traditional village cluster in Korea.

categories.name: Nightlife
categories.summary: Busan has Seomyeon and Gwangalli; Jeonju has makgeolli bars — charming but limited.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Busan is 40 min from Gyeongju. Jeonju's day trips require more effort.

categories.name: Getting There
categories.summary: Jeonju: 1h50m by KTX from Seoul. Busan: 2h30m.

categories.name: City Size
categories.summary: Jeonju is small and walkable. Busan is large and requires the subway.

faq.question: Is Jeonju or Busan better for first-time visitors?
faq.answer: Busan offers more variety; Jeonju is unmatched for food and traditional atmosphere. Most travelers do both.

faq.question: How do I get from Jeonju to Busan?
faq.answer: Intercity bus, 2.5–3 hours, 21,000–26,000 KRW ($15–19). No direct train.
